Hi Emily —

Thanks for the heads up and the runbook. Wed Nov 22 after 11am PT works on our side; we can also do Thu Nov 23 if you prefer the extra prep day.

High level on capacity:
- If you expect sustained 70–80 concurrent sessions during the 20-minute spike, Dedicated is the safer choice for the load test day — it guarantees GPU capacity and avoids noisy-neighbor throttles.
- Hosted can handle spikes with a quota bump and burst window for short load tests, but for the numbers you quoted I'd recommend a Dedicated reserve for the actual demo run and Hosted for the remainder of the POC.

Suggested next steps:
1) Pick the final date/time (Wed 11:30–13:00 PT or Thu 13:00–14:30 PT?)
2) Confirm target concurrency and acceptable failure percentage during the spike (we usually aim for <3% errored requests during demo runs)
3) Marcus will propose exact quota numbers and a rate-limit profile so you can request the Hosted bump if you want to avoid Dedicated.

I reviewed your capacity workbook — can you add a line with the expected number of multi-turn follow-ups per session? That shifts the token envelope materially.

On attachments: I saved your runbook and the workbook. I also created a short checklist for the lab prep (will attach the calendar invite once we lock timing).

- Lauren
Lauren Bishop

Lauren / Emily —

Quick technical note from infra: based on the numbers Emily shared, here are our conservative recommendations for the demo load window. These are tuned for Redwood's serving runtime characteristics (KV cache, batching, and model footprint).

Hosted (temporary bump):
- Token envelope: recommend 5M tokens/day for the trial window (to allow for pre-demo warmups + post-demo churn).
- Burst profile: allow 250 rps for 30 minutes during the spike with backoff policies (we'll enable 429 handling hints).
- Expected tail latency: 300–600ms per token on our verified medium-sized open models; throughput depends on prompt length and effective batching.

Dedicated (recommended for the spike):
- Reserve: 1 GPU cluster (x2 nodes) for the 60-minute window including warmup to keep effective concurrency low-latency.
- Rate limits: internal route at 400 rps sustained for 20 minutes; autoscaling disabled for the reserved window.
- Token budget: allocate ~7–8M tokens for the day to be safe if each attendee runs 3–4k tokens during the spike.

Operational items:
- If you go Hosted we need a HubSpot approval for quota bump (I can file the ticket once you confirm).
- If Dedicated, we need a signed short-form commitment for the day (we can provide the order form).
- Diego: can you prepare a quick test plan (3 warmup requests, capture latency distribution, and KV-cache priming steps)?

Happy to hop on a 15-min tech sync if that helps before the lab.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
